lines.text: September eighteen ninety-four. Swami Vivekananda has been in America for just over a year.
lines.ph: sɛptˈɛmbɚɹ ˈeɪtiːn nˈaɪntifˈoːɹ. swˈɑːmi vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə hˈæzbiːn ɪn ɐmˈɛɹɪkə fɔːɹ dʒˈʌst ˌoʊvɚɹ ɐ jˈɪɹ.

lines.text: He writes in Bengali to a friend in Madras, Manmatha Nath Bhattacharya.
lines.ph: hiː ɹˈaɪts ˈɪn bɛŋɡˈɔːli tʊ ɐ fɹˈɛnd ɪn mədɹˈɑːs, mˈʌnməθə nˈɑːt bˌʌtʃɑːtʃˈɑːɹjə.

lines.text: His friend has asked about a weaving machine, and the Swami promises to make inquiries and let him know.
lines.ph: hɪz fɹˈɛnd hɐz ˈæskt ɐbˌaʊt ɐ wˈiːvɪŋ məʃˈiːn, ænd ðˈə swˈɑːmi pɹˈɑːmɪsᵻz tə mˌeɪk ˈɪŋkwɚɹiz ænd lˈɛt hˌɪm nˈoʊ.

lines.text: For now he is resting at Annisquam, a village on the seacoast of Massachusetts.
lines.ph: fɔːɹ nˈaʊ hiː ɪz ɹˈɛstɪŋ æt ˈænɪskwɑːm, ɐ vˈɪlɪdʒ ɔnðə sˈiːkoʊst ʌv mˌæsɐtʃˈuːsɪts.

lines.text: Some come to bathe in the sea, some to take rest, and some to catch husbands.
lines.ph: sˌʌm kˈʌm tə bˈeɪð ɪnðə sˈiː, sˌʌm tə tˈeɪk ɹˈɛst, ænd sˌʌm tə kˈætʃ hˈʌsbəndz.

lines.text: What follows is one of his most candid letters: America and India, seen side by side.
lines.ph: wˌʌt fˈɑːloʊz ɪz wˈʌn ʌv hɪz mˈoʊst kˈændɪd lˈɛɾɚz: ɐmˈɛɹɪkə ænd ˈɪndiə, sˈiːn sˈaɪd baɪ sˈaɪd.

lines.text: There is a strong sense of decorum in this country, he writes.
lines.ph: ðɛɹ ɪz ɐ stɹˈɔŋ sˈɛns ʌv dᵻkˈoːɹəm ɪn ðɪs kˈʌntɹi, hiː ɹˈaɪts.

lines.text: In the presence of women you must always be covered from neck to foot, and the body's normal functions are never mentioned.
lines.ph: ɪnðə pɹˈɛzəns ʌv wˈɪmɪn juː mˈʌst ˈɔːlweɪz biː kˈʌvɚd fɹʌm nˈɛk tə fˈʊt, ænd ðə bˈɑːdiz nˈoːɹməl fˈʌŋkʃənz ɑːɹ nˈɛvɚ mˈɛnʃənd.

lines.text: You may blow your nose a thousand times into a handkerchief, but to belch is highly uncivilised.
lines.ph: juː mˈeɪ blˈoʊ jʊɹ nˈoʊz ɐ θˈaʊzənd tˈaɪmz ˌɪntʊ ɐ hˈændkɚtʃˌiːf, bˌʌt tə bˈɛltʃ ɪz hˈaɪli ʌnsˈɪvəlˌaɪzd.

lines.text: A low-cut evening gown is acceptable, yet to go barefoot is as bad as being naked.
lines.ph: ɐ lˈoʊkˈʌt ˈiːvnɪŋ ɡˈaʊn ɪz ɐksˈɛptəbəl, jˈɛt tə ɡˌoʊ bˈɛɹfʊt ɪz æz bˈæd æz bˌiːɪŋ nˈeɪkᵻd.

lines.text: Just as we always dwell on the soul, so they take care of the body.
lines.ph: dʒˈʌst æz wiː ˈɔːlweɪz dwˈɛl ɔnðə sˈoʊl, sˌoʊ ðeɪ tˈeɪk kˈɛɹ ʌvðə bˈɑːdi.

lines.text: There is no end to the cleaning and embellishing of it, and one who fails to do this has no place in society.
lines.ph: ðɛɹ ɪz nˈoʊ ˈɛnd tə ðə klˈiːnɪŋ ænd ɛmbˈɛlɪʃɪŋ ʌv ɪt, ænd wˈʌn hˌuː fˈeɪlz tə dˈuː ðɪs hɐz nˈoʊ plˈeɪs ɪn səsˈaɪəɾi.

lines.text: To Americans, cooking over cow-dung fuel and eating on the floor is eating like pigs. The very word is taboo in English.
lines.ph: tʊ ɐmˈɛɹɪkənz, kˈʊkɪŋ ˌoʊvɚ kˈaʊdˈʌŋ fjˈuːəl ænd ˈiːɾɪŋ ɔnðə flˈoːɹ ɪz ˈiːɾɪŋ lˈaɪk pˈɪɡz. ðə vˈɛɹi wˈɜːd ɪz tæbˈuː ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ.

lines.text: Yet many will drink from the same glass without washing it, and rarely wash things before cooking.
lines.ph: jˈɛt mˈɛni wɪl dɹˈɪŋk fɹʌmðə sˈeɪm ɡlˈæs wɪðˌaʊt wˈɑːʃɪŋ ɪt, ænd ɹˈɛɹli wˈɑːʃ θˈɪŋz bᵻfˌoːɹ kˈʊkɪŋ.

lines.text: But if the cook's clothes are a little soiled, she is thrown out.
lines.ph: bˌʌt ɪf ðə kˈʊks klˈoʊðz ɑːɹ ɐ lˈɪɾəl sˈɔɪld, ʃiː ɪz θɹˈoʊn ˈaʊt.

lines.text: The table-ware is all spick and span.
lines.ph: ðə tˈeɪbəlwˈɛɹ ɪz ˈɔːl spˈɪk ænd spˈæn.

lines.text: They are the richest people on earth; their enjoyments and luxuries beggar description.
lines.ph: ðeɪ ɑːɹ ðə ɹˈɪtʃɪst pˈiːpəl ˌɔn ˈɜːθ; ðɛɹ ɛndʒˈɔɪmənts ænd lˈʌkʃɚɹiz bˈɛɡɚ dᵻskɹˈɪpʃən.

lines.text: In Rajputana, he notes, people dine on a low seat with the plate on a low table, far better than a banana leaf on an earthen floor.
lines.ph: ˈɪn ɹˌɑːdʒpʊtˈɑːnə, hiː nˈoʊts, pˈiːpəl dˈaɪn ˌɔn ɐ lˈoʊ sˈiːt wɪððə plˈeɪt ˌɔn ɐ lˈoʊ tˈeɪbəl, fˈɑːɹ bˈɛɾɚ ðˌænə bɐnˈænə lˈiːf ˌɔn ɐn ˈɜːðən flˈoːɹ.

lines.text: Bengali women lose caste if they wear shoes; Rajput women lose caste if they do not. And Manu says, one shall always wear shoes.
lines.ph: bɛŋɡˈɔːli wˈɪmɪn lˈuːz kˈæst ɪf ðeɪ wˈɛɹ ʃˈuːz; ɹˈɑːdʒpʊt wˈɪmɪn lˈuːz kˈæst ɪf ðeɪ duːnˈɑːt. ˈænd mˈʌnuː sˈɛz, wˈʌn ʃˌæl ˈɔːlweɪz wˈɛɹ ʃˈuːz.

lines.text: People should have a decent standard of living: neat and clean, even if not luxurious.
lines.ph: pˈiːpəl ʃˌʊdəv ɐ dˈiːsənt stˈændɚd ʌv lˈɪvɪŋ: nˈiːt ænd klˈiːn, ˈiːvən ɪf nˌɑːt lʌɡʒˈʊɹɹiəs.

lines.text: Why do we have to be Englishmen? It is enough for the present if we imitate our brothers of the western provinces.
lines.ph: wˌaɪ dˈuː wiː hæv təbi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃmˌɛn? ɪɾ ɪz ɪnˈʌf fɚðə pɹˈɛzənt ɪf wiː ˈɪmᵻtˌeɪt ˌaʊɚ bɹˈʌðɚz ʌvðə wˈɛstɚn pɹˈɑːvɪnsᵻz.

lines.text: If group after group of Indians travel the world and come back, the face of India will change within twenty years.
lines.ph: ɪf ɡɹˈuːp ˈæftɚ ɡɹˈuːp ʌv ˈɪndiənz tɹˈævəl ðə wˈɜːld ænd kˈʌm bˈæk, ðə fˈeɪs ʌv ˈɪndiə wɪl tʃˈeɪndʒ wɪðˌɪn twˈɛnti jˈɪɹz.

lines.text: But how will anything happen if the people of one village do not visit the next? By and by, he writes, the stubborn Bengali boys will awaken the country.
lines.ph: bˌʌt hˌaʊ wɪl ˈɛnɪθˌɪŋ hˈæpən ɪf ðə pˈiːpəl ʌv wˈʌn vˈɪlɪdʒ duːnˌɑːt vˈɪzɪt ðə nˈɛkst? baɪ ænd bˈaɪ, hiː ɹˈaɪts, ðə stˈʌbɚn bɛŋɡˈɔːli bˈɔɪz wɪl ɐwˈeɪkən ðə kˈʌntɹi.

lines.text: Then he turns, sharply, to child marriage.
lines.ph: ðˈɛn hiː tˈɜːnz, ʃˈɑːɹpli, tə tʃˈaɪld mˈæɹɪdʒ.

lines.text: Manmatha Babu, you will have to stop this shameful business of marrying off nine-year-old girls. That is the root of all sins.
lines.ph: mˈʌnməθə bˈɑːbuː, juː wɪl hæv tə stˈɑːp ðɪs ʃˈeɪmfəl bˈɪznəs ʌv mˈæɹiɪŋ ˈɔf nˈaɪnjˈɪɹˈoʊld ɡˈɜːlz. ðæt ɪz ðə ɹˈuːt ʌv ˈɔːl sˈɪnz.

lines.text: When the government tried to pass a law against early marriage, our people raised a tremendous howl.
lines.ph: wˌɛn ðə ɡˈʌvɚnmənt tɹˈaɪd tə pˈæs ɐ lˈɔː ɐɡˈɛnst ˈɜːli mˈæɹɪdʒ, ˌaʊɚ pˈiːpəl ɹˈeɪzd ɐ tɹəmˈɛndəs hˈaʊl.

lines.text: If we do not stop it ourselves, he warns, the government will naturally intervene.
lines.ph: ɪf wiː duːnˌɑːt stˈɑːp ɪɾ aʊɚsˈɛlvz, hiː wˈɔːɹnz, ðə ɡˈʌvɚnmənt wɪl nˈætʃɚɹəli ˌɪntɚvˈiːn.

lines.text: Parents give a ten-year-old daughter in marriage to a full-grown man. All the world cries fie upon us.
lines.ph: pˈɛɹənts ɡˈɪv ɐ tˈɛnjˈɪɹˈoʊld dˈɔːɾɚɹ ɪn mˈæɹɪdʒ tʊ ɐ fˈʊlɡɹˈoʊn mˈæn. ˈɔːl ðə wˈɜːld kɹˈaɪz fˈaɪ əpˌɑːn ˌʌs.

lines.text: Is there any punishment without a sin? It is all the fruit of Karma, he says.
lines.ph: ɪz ðɛɹ ˌɛni pˈʌnɪʃmənt wɪðˌaʊt ɐ sˈɪn? ɪɾ ɪz ˈɔːl ðə fɹˈuːt ʌv kˈɑːɹmə, hiː sˈɛz.

lines.text: In America, the struggle over marriage falls on the girls, not the parents. It is the girls' job to capture husbands.
lines.ph: ɪn ɐmˈɛɹɪkə, ðə stɹˈʌɡəl ˌoʊvɚ mˈæɹɪdʒ fˈɔːlz ɔnðə ɡˈɜːlz, nˌɑːt ðə pˈɛɹənts. ɪɾ ɪz ðə ɡˈɜːlz dʒˈɑːb tə kˈæptʃɚ hˈʌsbəndz.

lines.text: He watches it all closely: I am, as it were, a woman amongst women.
lines.ph: hiː wˈɑːtʃᵻz ɪɾ ˈɔːl klˈoʊsli: aɪˈæm, æz ɪt wˈɜː, ɐ wˈʊmən ɐmˌʌŋst wˈɪmɪn.

lines.text: Dinners, dances, musical parties, the watering places; and all the while the young women scheme how to capture husbands.
lines.ph: dˈɪnɚz, dˈænsᵻz, mjˈuːzɪkəl pˈɑːɹɾiz, ðə wˈɔːɾɚɹɪŋ plˈeɪsᵻz; ænd ˈɔːl ðə wˈaɪl ðə jˈʌŋ wˈɪmɪn skˈiːm hˌaʊ tə kˈæptʃɚ hˈʌsbəndz.

lines.text: The boys flirt and slave for them, but the moment the girls reach out to catch them, they run away.
lines.ph: ðə bˈɔɪz flˈɜːt ænd slˈeɪv fɔːɹ ðˌɛm, bˌʌt ðə mˈoʊmənt ðə ɡˈɜːlz ɹˈiːtʃ ˈaʊt tə kˈætʃ ðˌɛm, ðeɪ ɹˈʌn ɐwˈeɪ.

lines.text: Money decides most matches, here as at home. One marriage in a thousand comes from love; then a quarrel, and divorce.
lines.ph: mˈʌni dᵻsˈaɪdz mˈoʊst mˈætʃᵻz, hˈɪɹ æz æt hˈoʊm. wˈʌn mˈæɹɪdʒ ɪn ɐ θˈaʊzənd kˈʌmz fɹʌm lˈʌv; ðˈɛn ɐ kwˈɔːɹəl, ænd dᵻvˈoːɹs.

lines.text: It is the same in all countries. The result is the same in either case.
lines.ph: ɪɾ ɪz ðə sˈeɪm ɪn ˈɔːl kˈʌntɹiz. ðə ɹɪzˈʌlt ɪz ðə sˈeɪm ɪn ˈiːðɚ kˈeɪs.

lines.text: Nowadays, he writes, American girls do not want to marry.
lines.ph: nˈaʊədˌeɪz, hiː ɹˈaɪts, ɐmˈɛɹɪkən ɡˈɜːlz duːnˌɑːt wˈɔnt tə mˈæɹi.

lines.text: During the Civil War so many men were killed that women began to do all kinds of work, and they have kept the rights they won.
lines.ph: dˈʊɹɹɪŋ ðə sˈɪvəl wˈɔːɹ sˌoʊ mˈɛni mˈɛn wɜː kˈɪld ðæt wˈɪmɪn bɪɡˈæn tə dˈuː ˈɔːl kˈaɪndz ʌv wˈɜːk, ænd ðeɪ hæv kˈɛpt ðə ɹˈaɪts ðeɪ wˈʌn.

lines.text: If we truly fall in love, then we shall marry; otherwise, we shall earn and meet our own expenses.
lines.ph: ɪf wiː tɹˈuːli fˈɔːl ɪn lˈʌv, ðˈɛn wiːʃˌɐl mˈæɹi; ˈʌðɚwˌaɪz, wiːʃˌɐl ˈɜːn ænd mˈiːt ˌaʊɚɹ ˈoʊn ɛkspˈɛnsᵻz.

lines.text: Even a millionaire's son must earn enough before he marries.
lines.ph: ˈiːvən ɐ mˌɪliənˈɛɹz sˈʌn mˈʌst ˈɜːn ɪnˈʌf bᵻfˌoːɹ hiː mˈæɹiz.

lines.text: When a girl marries, she brings her husband into her parents' home.
lines.ph: wˌɛn ɐ ɡˈɜːl mˈæɹiz, ʃiː bɹˈɪŋz hɜː hˈʌsbənd ˌɪntʊ hɜː pˈɛɹənts hˈoʊm.

lines.text: And in everything the husband here must say, Yes dear.
lines.ph: ænd ɪn ˈɛvɹɪθˌɪŋ ðə hˈʌsbənd hˈɪɹ mˈʌst sˈeɪ, jˈɛs dˈɪɹ.

lines.text: There are rivers of wealth here, he writes, waves of beauty, and an abundance of knowledge everywhere.
lines.ph: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ ɹˈɪvɚz ʌv wˈɛlθ hˈɪɹ, hiː ɹˈaɪts, wˈeɪvz ʌv bjˈuːɾi, ænd ɐn ɐbˈʌndəns ʌv nˈɑːlɪdʒ ˈɛvɹɪwˌɛɹ.

lines.text: The women are sentimental, with a mania for romance.
lines.ph: ðə wˈɪmɪn ɑːɹ sˌɛntɪmˈɛntəl, wɪð ɐ mˈeɪniə fɔːɹ ɹoʊmˈæns.

lines.text: I am, however, a strange sort of animal who hasn't any romantic feeling.
lines.ph: aɪˈæm, haʊˈɛvɚ, ɐ stɹˈeɪndʒ sˈɔːɹt ʌv ˈænɪməl hˌuː hˈæzənt ˌɛni ɹoʊmˈæntɪk fˈiːlɪŋ.

lines.text: So they show him great respect. He makes them all call him father, or brother.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ ðeɪ ʃˈoʊ hˌɪm ɡɹˈeɪt ɹᵻspˈɛkt. hiː mˌeɪks ðˌɛm ˈɔːl kˈɔːl hˌɪm fˈɑːðɚ, ɔːɹ bɹˈʌðɚ.

lines.text: Of the unmarried girls, he says, they are exceedingly good, because their future is bright.
lines.ph: ʌvðɪ ʌnmˈæɹid ɡˈɜːlz, hiː sˈɛz, ðeɪ ɑːɹ ɛksˈiːdɪŋli ɡˈʊd, bɪkˈʌz ðɛɹ fjˈuːtʃɚɹ ɪz bɹˈaɪt.

lines.text: Many American women are very well educated, and put many a learned professor to shame.
lines.ph: mˈɛni ɐmˈɛɹɪkən wˈɪmɪn ɑːɹ vˈɛɹi wˈɛl ˈɛdʒuːkˌeɪɾᵻd, ænd pˌʊt mˈɛni ɐ lˈɜːnᵻd pɹəfˈɛsɚ tə ʃˈeɪm.

lines.text: And what kindness, what noble thought and action! In the best houses he is treated like their own son.
lines.ph: ænd wʌt kˈaɪndnəs, wˌʌt nˈoʊbəl θˈɔːt ænd ˈækʃən! ɪnðə bˈɛst hˈaʊzᵻz hiː ɪz tɹˈiːɾᵻd lˈaɪk ðɛɹ ˈoʊn sˈʌn.

lines.text: A young woman is gathering information about the weaving machine for him; the girls arranged a phonograph for the Maharaja of Khetri.
lines.ph: ɐ jˈʌŋ wˈʊmən ɪz ɡˈæðɚɹɪŋ ˌɪnfɚmˈeɪʃən ɐbˌaʊt ðə wˈiːvɪŋ məʃˈiːn fɔːɹ hˌɪm; ðə ɡˈɜːlz ɚɹˈeɪndʒd ɐ fˈɑːnəɡɹˌæf fɚðə mˌɑːhəɹˈɑːdʒə ˈʌv kˈeɪtɹi.

lines.text: They are the goddess Lakshmi in beauty and the goddess Saraswati in talents and accomplishments.
lines.ph: ðeɪ ɑːɹ ðə ɡˈɑːdəs lˈʌkʃmi ɪn bjˈuːɾi ænd ðə ɡˈɑːdəs sˈʌɹəsvəti ɪn tˈælənts ænd ɐkˈɑːmplɪʃmənts.

lines.text: This cannot be achieved through books, he says. Can you send out men and women to see the world?
lines.ph: ðɪs kænˈɑːt biː ɐtʃˈiːvd θɹuː bˈʊks, hiː sˈɛz. kæn juː sˈɛnd ˈaʊt mˈɛn ænd wˈɪmɪn tə sˈiː ðə wˈɜːld?

lines.text: The men here are clever at earning wealth. Where others do not see even dust, there they see gold.
lines.ph: ðə mˈɛn hˈɪɹ ɑːɹ klˈɛvɚɹ æɾ ˈɜːnɪŋ wˈɛlθ. wˌɛɹ ˈʌðɚz duːnˌɑːt sˈiː ˈiːvən dˈʌst, ðɛɹ ðeɪ sˈiː ɡˈoʊld.

lines.text: Then he breaks into English.
lines.ph: ðˈɛn hiː bɹˈeɪks ˌɪntʊ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ.

lines.text: Keeping aloof from the community of nations is the only cause for the downfall of India.
lines.ph: kˈiːpɪŋ ɐlˈuːf fɹʌmðə kəmjˈuːnᵻɾi ʌv nˈeɪʃənz ɪz ðɪ ˈoʊnli kˈɔːz fɚðə dˈaʊnfɔːl ʌv ˈɪndiə.

lines.text: Since the English came, India has been forced back into the company of nations, and is visibly rising again.
lines.ph: sˈɪns ðɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ kˈeɪm, ˈɪndiə hˈæzbiːn fˈoːɹst bˈæk ˌɪntʊ ðə kˈʌmpəni ʌv nˈeɪʃənz, ænd ɪz vˈɪzᵻbli ɹˈaɪzɪŋ ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: Everyone who goes out of the country benefits the whole nation, for that is how its horizon expands. And because women cannot go, they have made almost no progress.
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn hˌuː ɡoʊz ˌaʊɾəv ðə kˈʌntɹi bˈɛnɪfˌɪts ðə hˈoʊl nˈeɪʃən, fɔːɹ ðæt ɪz hˌaʊ ɪts hɚɹˈaɪzən ɛkspˈændz. ænd bɪkˈʌz wˈɪmɪn kænˈɑːt ɡˈoʊ, ðeɪ hæv mˌeɪd ˈɔːlmoʊst nˈoʊ pɹˈɑːɡɹɛs.

lines.text: There is no station of rest; either you progress upwards or you go back and die out.
lines.ph: ðɛɹ ɪz nˈoʊ stˈeɪʃən ʌv ɹˈɛst; ˈiːðɚ juː pɹəɡɹˈɛs ˈʌpwɚdz ɔːɹ juː ɡˌoʊ bˈæk ænd dˈaɪ ˈaʊt.

lines.text: The only sign of life is going outward and forward and expansion. Contraction is death.
lines.ph: ðɪ ˈoʊnli sˈaɪn ʌv lˈaɪf ɪz ɡˌoʊɪŋ ˈaʊtwɚd ænd fˈɔːɹwɚd ænd ɛkspˈænʃən. kəntɹˈækʃən ɪz dˈɛθ.

lines.text: Why do good to others? Because it is the only condition of life: you expand beyond your little self, and live and grow.
lines.ph: wˌaɪ dˈuː ɡˈʊd tʊ ˈʌðɚz? bɪkˈʌz ɪɾ ɪz ðɪ ˈoʊnli kəndˈɪʃən ʌv lˈaɪf: juː ɛkspˈænd bᵻjˌɔnd jʊɹ lˈɪɾəl sˈɛlf, ænd lˈaɪv ænd ɡɹˈoʊ.

lines.text: All narrowness, all contraction, all selfishness is simply slow suicide.
lines.ph: ˈɔːl nˈæɹoʊnəs, ˈɔːl kəntɹˈækʃən, ˈɔːl sˈɛlfɪʃnəs ɪz sˈɪmpli slˈoʊ sˈuːɪsˌaɪd.

lines.text: Women too must go forward. Who would break this horrible crystallisation of death? Lord help us!
lines.ph: wˈɪmɪn tˈuː mˈʌst ɡˌoʊ fˈɔːɹwɚd. hˌuː wʊd bɹˈeɪk ðɪs hˈɔːɹɪbəl kɹˌɪstɐləzˈeɪʃən ʌv dˈɛθ? lˈɔːɹd hˈɛlp ˌʌs!

lines.text: Yet change will come gradually, and he quotes a Bengali saying.
lines.ph: jˈɛt tʃˈeɪndʒ wɪl kˈʌm ɡɹˈædʒuːəli, ænd hiː kwˈoʊts ˈeɪ bɛŋɡˈɔːli sˈeɪɪŋ.

lines.text: One should cross a road slowly and cautiously; one should patch a quilt carefully and cautiously; so should one be slow and cautious in crossing a mountain.
lines.ph: wˈʌn ʃˌʊd kɹˈɔs ɐ ɹˈoʊd slˈoʊli ænd kˈɔːʃəsli; wˈʌn ʃˌʊd pˈætʃ ɐ kwˈɪlt kˈɛɹfəli ænd kˈɔːʃəsli; sˌoʊ ʃˌʊd wˈʌn biː slˈoʊ ænd kˈɔːʃəs ɪn kɹˈɔsɪŋ ɐ mˈaʊntɪn.

lines.text: The papers from India have arrived, he reports, and the enemy has been silenced.
lines.ph: ðə pˈeɪpɚz fɹʌm ˈɪndiə hæv ɚɹˈaɪvd, hiː ɹᵻpˈoːɹts, ænd ðɪ ˈɛnəmi hˈæzbiːn sˈaɪlənst.

lines.text: A fellow countryman, Mazoomdar, has been calling him a rogue, but no one pays attention.
lines.ph: ɐ fˈɛloʊ kˈʌntɹɪmən, məzˈuːmdɑːɹ, hˈæzbiːn kˈɔːlɪŋ hˌɪm ɐ ɹˈoʊɡ, bˌʌt nˈoʊwˈʌn pˈeɪz ɐtˈɛnʃən.

lines.text: These people let an unknown young man live among their families. I am like a foster son to the American women; they are really my mother.
lines.ph: ðiːz pˈiːpəl lˈɛt ɐn ʌnnˈoʊn jˈʌŋ mˈæn lˈaɪv ɐmˌʌŋ ðɛɹ fˈæmɪliz. aɪɐm lˈaɪk ɐ fˈɑːstɚ sˈʌn tə ðɪ ɐmˈɛɹɪkən wˈɪmɪn; ðeɪ ɑːɹ ɹˈiəli maɪ mˈʌðɚ.

lines.text: A while back, several hundred intellectual men and women gathered at a place called Greenacre, in Maine, and he stayed nearly two months.
lines.ph: ɐ wˈaɪl bˈæk, sˈɛvɹəl hˈʌndɹɪd ˌɪntəlˈɛktʃuːəl mˈɛn ænd wˈɪmɪn ɡˈæðɚd æɾə plˈeɪs kˈɔːld ɡɹˈiːneɪkɚ, ɪn mˈeɪn, ænd hiː stˈeɪd nˌɪɹli tˈuː mˈʌnθs.

lines.text: Every day he sat in the Hindu fashion under a tree, and his followers sat on the grass all around him.
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹi dˈeɪ hiː sˈæt ɪnðə hˈɪnduː fˈæʃən ˌʌndɚɹ ɐ tɹˈiː, ænd hɪz fˈɑːloʊɚz sˈæt ɔnðə ɡɹˈæs ˈɔːl ɚɹˈaʊnd hˌɪm.

lines.text: Every morning he taught them. How earnest they were!
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹi mˈɔːɹnɪŋ hiː tˈɔːt ðˌɛm. hˌaʊ ˈɜːnɪst ðeɪ wɜː!

lines.text: The whole country now knows him. Some ministers are angry, though many learned ministers follow him.
lines.ph: ðə hˈoʊl kˈʌntɹi nˈaʊ nˈoʊz hˌɪm. sˌʌm mˈɪnɪstɚz ɑːɹ ˈæŋɡɹi, ðˌoʊ mˈɛni lˈɜːnᵻd mˈɪnɪstɚz fˈɑːloʊ hˌɪm.

lines.text: I have been adopted by them, he writes.
lines.ph: aɪ hɐvbɪn ɐdˈɑːptᵻd baɪ ðˌɛm, hiː ɹˈaɪts.

lines.text: When will he return to India? Possibly next winter. There I shall have to wander, and here also I do the same.
lines.ph: wˌɛn wɪl hiː ɹᵻtˈɜːn tʊ ˈɪndiə? pˈɑːsᵻbli nˈɛkst wˈɪntɚ. ðɛɹ aɪʃˌɐl hæv tə wˈɔndɚ, ænd hˈɪɹ ˈɔːlsoʊ aɪ dˈuː ðə sˈeɪm.

lines.text: Then a last request: please don't make this letter public.
lines.ph: ðˈɛn ɐ lˈæst ɹᵻkwˈɛst: plˈiːz dˈoʊnt mˌeɪk ðɪs lˈɛɾɚ pˈʌblɪk.

lines.text: I have to be careful about every word I say. I am now a public man. Everybody is watching.
lines.ph: aɪ hæv təbi kˈɛɹfəl ɐbˌaʊt ˈɛvɹi wˈɜːd aɪ sˈeɪ. aɪɐm nˈaʊ ɐ pˈʌblɪk mˈæn. ˈɛvɹɪbˌɑːdi ɪz wˈɑːtʃɪŋ.

lines.text: Yours faithfully, Vivekananda.
lines.ph: jˈoːɹz fˈeɪθfəli, vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə.
